text:
Marta: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a runtime 'hotplug' path for swapping weight shards without full model restart. Posting rough design + questions.

Josh: Nice. Quick question: what happens to in-flight KV/cache pointers? We can't flip while GPU is reading memory.

Marta: Plan is atomic pointer flip + refcount-style lifetime for old buffers. New requests see new ptr, in-flight reads complete against old memory until refcount reaches 0 then free. Keep locks minimal.

Li: Refcounts on GPU buffers are awkward. Suggest using per-shard epoch counters and a lightweight per-request epoch stamp instead of full refcounts. Bump epoch on new version, drain old epoch with grace window.

Marta: Yep — epoch bumping is the primary idea. Request attaches epoch at start. If it observes old epoch, it will continue using old ptr. GC runs once last-seen epoch is cleared or a timeout happens.

Ana: How do we avoid inconsistency for long-lived conversations? If weights shift mid-conversation outputs could diverge unpredictably.

Marta: We'll pin model version at request start for any request that depends on prefix state. Streaming responses will include a model_version header; if a later chunk would require an incompatible kernel we fallback to safe-mode or a compatible variant and emit telemetry.

Josh: Backpressure: if we need to swap under load and hosts are already saturated, swaps could cause OOM / slowdown. How do we gate swaps?

Marta: Swaps should be gated by host load and a prefetch budget. We transfer new copy in background into ephemeral buffers. Pointer flip only when all shards are resident and integrity checks pass. If system load is high we postpone commit or do canary commit to a small % of traffic.

Li: For sharded checkpoints we need a rendezvous to ensure all shards arrive before flip. Two-phase: transfer -> checksum/parse -> commit. That avoids partial visibility.

Ana: Two-phase commit is heavy for fast rollouts. Could we do optimistic flip + integrity probe + rollback? Rollbacks after serving are messy.

Marta: Agreed — rollbacks are painful. Prefer guarantee that no flip happens until everything is sanity-checked. For low-risk changes we can use canary lanes first.

prefetch-bot: prefetch-bot: transfer-start model=redwood-3-small shard=2 host=host-17

Josh: Does safetensors support streaming into GPU while verifying headers? We prefer to avoid a full copy when possible.

Marta: safetensors supports chunked reads. We'll prefetch critical layers (attention, KV) first so warmup can begin early. Non-critical layers can stream in lazily. If on-the-fly quant fallback is needed, we do an ephemeral decode then copy.

Li: Eviction interplay: if a shard is being prefetched we must pin it from eviction until commit done. Otherwise we risk GC during transfer. Use a lease/pin token tied to the transfer lifecycle.

Marta: Exactly — pin-on-prefetch, release after commit+GC. Lease length configurable; can shorten under pressure.

Ana: Edge-case: manifestless bundles (multiple shards in a single file). How do we hot-swap one logical shard without copying the whole archive?

Marta: We'll expose a per-shard index with byte ranges for bundled files. For atomicity we may need to copy the required ranges to an ephemeral aligned buffer, then memory-map / zero-copy to GPU if the filesystem supports it.

Josh: API changes needed for loader: begin_hotplug(shard, version, prefetch_budget), probe_integrity(), commit_hotplug(), abort_hotplug() — plus a pin_for_request(req_id, shards[]) to pin versions during request lifetime.

Marta: I'm proposing those exact call names in the RFC follow-up. Also need a hook to mark kernel-compatibility: can_kernel_run(model_version, kernel_version) before commit.

Li: Telemetry is essential: swaps/sec, aborted_swaps, average_drain_time_ms, bytes_moved, commit_latency, and version_skew_incidents. We should alert on skew > X seconds.

Ana: Add a safety toggle for dedicated/reserved customers to disable hotplug entirely (enterprise safety mode).

Marta: Good call. Also need a compatibility shim for older safetensors loaders that don't expose chunk checksums — fallback to full-verify copy then commit.

prefetch-bot: prefetch-bot: transfer-complete model=redwood-3-small shard=2 host=host-17 duration_ms=3124 checksum=ok

Josh: I'll run a matrix of load tests once the proto is in. Interested in swap latency vs QPS and tail-latency impact.

Marta: Thanks — I'll draft RFC follow-up with pseudo-code for epoch bumping, two-phase transfer, pin/lease semantics, and a small benchmark. Will include example failure modes and graceful-degradation paths.

Li: Couple of micro-safety notes to include: make GC triggered by both refcount and wallclock TTL, and ensure that any rollback path emits a hazard event to SRE.

Ana: :thumbsup: Sync tomorrow 10am PT?

Marta: Yes, putting on calendar. Thanks all.
